questions.prompt: What is a trigger in Azure Functions?

options.text: The single event that starts a function running
The billing plan for the function app

questions.explanation: Every function has exactly one trigger — the event (HTTP request, timer, queue message, new blob, etc.) that starts it. Bindings then connect it to data.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the Consumption plan are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: It scales automatically, including to zero when idle
It can have cold starts and a maximum execution time
It's ideal for long-running, always-on processes

questions.explanation: Consumption scales to zero, bills per run, and can cold-start with a time limit. Long-running, always-on work is a poor fit — use Premium/Dedicated or another service.

questions.prompt: The short startup delay when a new instance spins up after the function has been idle is called a cold ____.
questions.explanation: A cold start is the startup delay after idle. The Premium plan avoids it by keeping instances pre-warmed.

questions.prompt: Order the flow of a blob-triggered function that writes a result.

items.text: An output binding writes the result

questions.explanation: An event (new blob) fires the trigger, the function runs, and an output binding writes the result — with little glue code.

questions.prompt: Match each Functions concept to its meaning.

pairs.right: The event that starts a function
Scales to zero, bills per execution

questions.explanation: Trigger starts the function; bindings connect to data; Consumption scales to zero; Premium stays warm.
